title: High fire risk could trigger PG&E power shutoffs in parts of Bay Area
text:
According to the utility, parts of Napa, Sonoma and Solano counties could be affected by the planned outages.
Rising temperatures across the Bay Area are prompting fire weather concerns and the possibility of PG&E Public Safety Power Shutoffs. Christie Smith reports. Rising temperatures across the Bay Area are prompting fire weather concerns and the possibility of PG&E Public Safety Power Shutoffs.
A Red Flag Warning is set to take effect starting 11 p.m. Wednesday as hot, dry and windy conditions increase wildfire risk across parts of Northern California, including parts of the East Bay Hills and the North Bay interior mountains. PG&E said it is on alert and warned that emergency power shutoffs are possible in some areas to reduce the risk of wildfire caused by electrical equipment.
According to the utility, parts of Napa, Sonoma and Solano counties could be affected by the planned outages. PG&E is urging customers in affected areas to prepare for the possibility of outages and monitor updates from the utility as weather conditions evolve.
“Right now, we have notified customers in parts of the North Bay of the possibility of they may be in the footprint of a PSPS if one is called, so that area is really select small areas of Napa and Sonoma counties,” PG&E Spokesperson Tamar Sarkissian said. In the meantime, firefighters with the Contra Costa County Fire Protection District are monitoring the situation.
“What that means for us is operationally we got to have a dynamic approach to our staffing, we’re going to upstaff our hand crew overnight which includes about 22 personnel, including a water tender we have our dozer operators that are on stand by, which is staffed,” Contra Costa County Fire Protection District Assistant Chief of Operations Dominic Ciotola said. “We are seeing the fire activity high for this year its traveling pretty quickly once we are getting those fires so we are trying to make sure that we stop enough to make sure that we can contain those relatively quickly,” he said.
Later on in the day, Contra Costa County Fire crews stopped forward progress on a vegetation fire in Martinez. In Oakland, the fire department is also planning on staffing up overnight and closing some park space as a precaution.
Oakland Fire Department spokesperson Michael Hunt explained that while Oakland Parks are generally closed overnight, the department and the city are closing Joaquin Miller Park from 6 a.m. Thursday morning to 11 a.m. Oakland Fire will also have crews patrolling overnight, discouraging behavior that could spark a fire.
"Obviously, you wouldn’t want to discard any tobacco products , we would advise people against, particularly in the later hours, barbecuing or doing any grilling activity that could potentially create any spark or ember along the hillside," Hunt said. "We do often find cars double-parked or cars parked along roadsides along Grizzly Peak and Skyline Boulevard that could be smoking or participating in some other activity that could potentially cause an ignition source or some type of potential hazard," he continued.
Hunt added that it's important for people parking along roads to leave room for emergency vehicles to get through if they need to.
